context: Authentication has moved from strict single-use refresh-token invalidation to bounded previous-token grace. Immediate invalidation was rejected after concurrency tests confirmed legitimate near-simultaneous refresh requests. The current implementation preserves replay protection outside the grace interval. Unit and integration behavior is stable; the remaining question is whether previous-token state must move to shared storage when auth workers are horizontally scaled.

architecture: Refresh tokens rotate with one immediately previous token accepted only during a bounded grace interval.
decisions: Strict immediate invalidation is not compatible with observed client retry concurrency.
constraints: Replay outside the grace interval must remain rejected.
open_work: Confirm distributed storage strategy for multi-instance deployments.

next_steps: Inspect production topology and move grace state to Redis if requests can land on different auth workers.
